proposal.root_problem: Refund requests are failing to complete because payment-db rejects them at IBAN format validation (5/5 refund_failures records = FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01); customers wait indefinitely for an outcome that cannot occur until this backend validation/data issue is fixed, and this delay is independent of support's ticket response speed, which is already fast (E-02).
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds.
symptoms: Customers wait a long time for a resolution on refund inquiries (CL-01, CL-02).
All 5 payment-db refund_failures records are stuck in status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01).
Support ticket response times are already fast (2.0h median vs 24h SLA over 900 tickets, E-02), ruling out slow support as the cause.
causal_chain: Customers submit refund requests whose IBANs fail payment-db's format validation (E-01: 5/5 refund_failures records show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT).
These refunds are rejected at the payment-system validation step and never reach completion, regardless of support's response speed (E-01 interpretation).
Customers perceive indefinite waiting because the underlying refund never resolves, and support (SH-SUP) reframes this as a missing automated response channel (CL-01/CL-02, E-03).
Ticket-db shows support already answers inquiries quickly (2.0h median vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02), so the wait is not caused by slow support response and a chatbot would not fix it.

assumptions.statement: The 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records in payment-db are assumed to be representative of the refund delays driving the support backlog complaint, though total refund volume and the ticket-to-refund link are not established.
IBAN format validation failures are assumed to require a data or process correction rather than being a transient tool glitch, based on E-01's interpretation.

key_points: The stakeholder (SH-SUP) requested a chatbot to stop customers waiting for refund answers (CL-01, CL-02), but this framing was tested against evidence, not taken as the problem.

payment-db shows all 5 refund_failures records stuck at status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, fact F-01), while ticket-db shows support already answers tickets fast - 2.0h median vs a 24h SLA over 900 tickets (E-02, fact F-02).

This evidence rejected the 'no chatbot/slow response' hypothesis (H-RESPONSE-CHANNEL-GAP, contradicted by E-01 and E-02) and also rejected H-TICKET-VOLUME-OVERLOAD and H-PAYMENT-TICKET-DATA-SILO, while supporting H-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILURE (SUPPORTED by E-01, E-02).
The root problem (PD-1) was therefore redefined as: refunds fail to complete because payment-db rejects them at IBAN format validation, independent of support response speed, per E-01 and E-02.

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring three critical/high unknowns (U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE, U-DATA-COMPLETENESS, U-BANK-API-ACCESS-BLOCKED) to verification obligations (VOBs) that remain OPEN but whose blocking scope falls outside what is actually being released.

What is released is the minimum-useful-scope item 'monitor_refund_failure_rate' on DA-PAY (work item W-WI-01, DONE), which produces a monitoring dataset/metric (M-IBAN-FAILURE-COUNT, currently 5) for the FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT backlog - not a chatbot and not a fix to the IBAN failures themselves.

The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no hold items, meaning the monitoring capability goes out now while deeper diagnosis/remediation work (investigate_iban_validation_failures, cross_reference_failed_refunds_with_tickets, determine_iban_failure_root_cause) remains unfinished because it is blocked by open VOBs and a degraded tool.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS: three unknowns were deferred as VOBs rather than resolved before release (VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE, VOB-U-DATA-COMPLETENESS, VOB-U-BANK-API-ACCESS-BLOCKED), and all three remain OPEN even though the release went ahead because their blocking scope sits outside what was actually released.

It is not confirmed that the 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records (E-01) represent the full set of refund delays behind the complaint, because completeness of DA-PAY and DA-TCK is UNKNOWN (unknown U-DATA-COMPLETENESS); the investigation and cross-referencing work needed to answer this is blocked and unfinished.

The specific root cause of the IBAN failures - a validation-logic defect, bad customer-entered data, or a genuine processing delay - is still undetermined (unknown U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE, CRITICAL), and H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY remains an uneliminated candidate alongside H-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILURE, so success criterion SC-ROOT-CAUSE-IDENTIFIED is not met by what was released.

Diagnosis is further constrained because the bank-api tool is DEGRADED with an ACCESS_DENIED, non-transient hold and no fallback path, blocking the settlement-status checks needed to resolve the root cause (unknown U-BANK-API-ACCESS-BLOCKED); this is outside the process's control within the remaining time budget.

A chatbot or automated response channel, the originally requested solution, will not resolve the backlog because the delay originates in backend payment validation, not response latency - this is an explicit stated limitation of the release.

The targeted fix (a validation-logic patch or an IBAN data-correction workflow) that would actually remove the root cause has not been designed or applied, and depends on first confirming which specific cause (validation defect, bad data, or processing delay) is at play.
proposal.summary: The requester (SH-SUP) initially asked for a chatbot to stop customers waiting on refund answers (CL-01, CL-02), but evidence contradicted that framing: payment-db shows all 5 sampled refund_failures stuck at FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01), while ticket-db shows support already responds fast (2.0h median vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02). This supported H-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILURE and rejected the response-channel-gap, ticket-volume-overload, and data-silo hypotheses, redefining the root problem (PD-1) as a backend IBAN-validation failure blocking refund completion, independent of support speed. The DEFINE gate returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring three unknowns (root cause of the IBAN failures, data completeness of DA-PAY/DA-TCK, and bank-api access) as open verification obligations whose blocking scope lies outside this release. What was actually released is the minimum-useful-scope item monitor_refund_failure_rate on DA-PAY (work item W-WI-01, DONE), producing a monitoring metric for the FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT backlog - not a chatbot and not a fix. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no held items: the monitoring capability ships now, while deeper investigation, cross-referencing, root-cause determination, and any actual remediation remain unfinished, blocked by the open VOBs, the degraded bank-api tool, and an uneliminated competing hypothesis (H-REFUND-PROCESSING-DELAY).
